units.unit: The student wants to understand the debate over rent control for subdivided flats in Hong Kong.
The student asks for sources to be pulled together.
The student has no claim yet and wants to figure out the actual problem.
The student asks what the current law already does about rents in these units.
The student asks where the current law seems to fall short.
The student wants something on the existing ordinance and how it works in practice.
The student wants the existing ordinance and its real-world limits.
The student finds the primer and enforcement minute especially useful.
The student is missing the empirical backbone.
The student asks for material on supply elasticity of small rental units.
The student asks for modelled scenarios of what a rent cap does to the number of units and who gets excluded.
The student asks for comparisons of Hong Kong with other cities that tried first-generation rent freezes, like Berlin or New York.
The source would stand behind the sentence that a hard cap shrinks the stock future tenants rely on.
The student needs a source with actual elasticity estimates for small rental units.
The student needs a modelled scenario showing how many households get priced out.
The student wants a second source comparing Hong Kong with first-generation freezes like Berlin or New York.
The student wants to see whether the contraction shows up in those comparative cases too.
The student wants empirical elasticity, comparative cases, and tenant survey material.
The student wants to check how the comparative notes characterise first-rent versus increase-based controls rather than assuming they line up.
The student plans to read the New York note more closely as the case that supposedly shows a lighter scheme behaving differently.
